FINDING_ID: LB_F001
SEVERITY: 0.91
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.78
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager.get_allocation()` claims allocation uses LIVE fingerprints and adapts to observed capability, but those live fingerprints never reach `LoadBalancer`. `get_live_models()` builds `ModelSpec`s with updated `fingerprint`, yet `LoadBalancer` ignores `ModelSpec.fingerprint` entirely: `_solve_greedy()`, `_objective()`, and `_admissibility_mask()` use only token demand, limits, costs, latency, and roles. So the adaptive-routing feedback loop is functionally disconnected on the load-balancing path: fingerprint updates can affect `RoleAssignment.reassign()`, but not actual task-to-model allocation. That makes the public behavior claim materially false and leaves Area 2 unable to route work by demonstrated capability.
PROPOSED_FIX: Thread capability into Area 2 explicitly. At minimum, define a task-model suitability score using `Task.flaw_class` and `ModelSpec.fingerprint`/capability data, and use it in `_solve_greedy()` tie-breaking or as part of `_objective()`. If capability routing is intentionally out of scope for load balancing, remove the claim from `DynamicManager.get_allocation()` and document that live fingerprints currently affect only role reassignment.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: LB_F002
SEVERITY: 0.84
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.66
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager.get_allocation()` returns only `(Allocation, cost, balanced)` and discards the `LoadBalancer` instance that holds `_allocation_warnings`. Even if a caller wanted to inspect degraded redundancy, impossible targets, or forced overload situations, that state is inaccessible through the manager API. This is distinct from the already-known issue that `LoadBalancer.solve()` hides warnings internally: the top-level orchestration interface also suppresses degradation state, so manager clients cannot make recovery decisions based on allocation quality.
PROPOSED_FIX: Introduce a structured allocation result type returned by both `LoadBalancer.solve()` and `DynamicManager.get_allocation()`, e.g. `AllocationResult(allocation, cost, balanced, feasible, violations, warnings)`. Short of that, expose the active `LoadBalancer` warnings through the manager return path or event stream.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: LB_F003
SEVERITY: 0.76
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.57
DESCRIPTION: `LoadBalancer.solve()` does not reset `self._allocation_warnings` before solving. Since `_solve_greedy()` appends to this list, repeated calls to `solve()` on the same `LoadBalancer` instance accumulate stale warnings from prior solves. That contaminates current allocation diagnostics with historical state and can falsely suggest degradation in a later solve that was actually clean.
PROPOSED_FIX: Clear `self._allocation_warnings` at the start of `solve()` or `_solve_greedy()`. Better, make warnings local to a single solve and return them in an immutable result object instead of storing mutable cross-call state on the balancer.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: LB_F004
SEVERITY: 0.73
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.61
DESCRIPTION: `RoleAssignment.reassign()` accepts `round_idx` but never uses it. The docstring says reassignment is “between rounds” and the argument is “for failure history,” implying round-sensitive behavior, yet the implementation applies a lifetime-average failure penalty over all recorded history with no round scoping. This is an interface/contract defect in the load-balancing control path: callers are led to believe reassignment is round-aware when it is not.
PROPOSED_FIX: Either remove `round_idx` from the signature and docstring, or actually use it to compute a round-bounded/history-windowed failure penalty aligned to the current round.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: LB_F005
SEVERITY: 0.71
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.64
DESCRIPTION: `RoleAssignment.reassign()` can return a `role_map` containing `self.pm_model_id: Role.PM` even when the PM is not in `active_models`. The method unconditionally seeds `new_map` with the locked PM, then assigns remaining active models around it. That means downstream consumers can receive a role map mixing inactive and active models, despite reassignment ostensibly operating on the active pool. In load-balancing terms this preserves a ghost PM role in the control state and forces later components to work around it.
PROPOSED_FIX: Validate at entry that `pm_model_id` is active if reassignment is being performed; otherwise either abort, or return a role map over active models only while signaling that the locked PM is unavailable. At minimum, document this invariant explicitly and enforce it with a check.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: LB_F006
SEVERITY: 0.62
FLAW_CLASS: 6
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.41
DESCRIPTION: `feasibility_probability()` can return NaN or raise undefined-behavior-style math results for finite-looking but invalid inputs such as `task_load = NaN` or `model.L_std = NaN`. The method only branches on `model.L_std <= 0`; with NaN, that comparison is false, so it computes `z = (L - task_load) / L_std`, producing NaN, and then returns NaN from `math.erf`. `dispatch_check()` then compares `NaN >= threshold`, which is always false, silently blocking dispatch with a non-probability. This is a concrete edge-case bug in dispatch feasibility handling.
PROPOSED_FIX: Validate `model.L`, `model.L_std`, and `task_load` for finiteness at the start of `feasibility_probability()`. Reject NaN/inf inputs with `ValueError`, or coerce to a safe fallback and emit an explicit warning/event.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: LB_F007
SEVERITY: 0.58
FLAW_CLASS: 8
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.34
DESCRIPTION: The `feasibility_probability()` docstring states the return is a “Probability in [0, 1],” but the implementation does not enforce that for malformed floating inputs and can return NaN. That makes the API contract false even if normal inputs usually behave. In a load-balancing/dispatch gate, documentation that promises a probability but can yield NaN is misleading.
PROPOSED_FIX: Either enforce the documented contract with input validation and clamping to `[0, 1]`, or update the docstring to state the preconditions: finite `L`, `L_std`, and `task_load`.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: LB_F008
SEVERITY: 0.67
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.52
DESCRIPTION: `RoleAssignment.get_ordering()` sorts only by score and omits the deterministic tie-break used in `assign()`. For homogeneous or score-tied models, the returned capability ordering depends on dict insertion order rather than the declared tie-break semantics `(A, v_bar, 1-D_decay, C)`. Since orderings are part of role-allocation introspection, this makes the exported ordering inconsistent with actual assignment policy.
PROPOSED_FIX: Sort with the same secondary key used by assignment, e.g. carry a `model_id -> ModelSpec` map and order by `(score, _tie_break_key(model))` descending.
VERIFIED: TRUE
